newsitem.title: UK: Russian debt resilient after Ukraine delays deal.
newsitem.headline: Russian debt resilient after Ukraine delays deal.

text.p: Russian debt prices shrugged off news on Wednesday that the Ukraine had delayed ratification of a deal with Russia over claims to Soviet assets.
Ukraine's parliament delayed ratification of a deal with Russia under which Kiev would renounce claims to Soviet assets in return for Moscow's assuming Ukraine's share of Soviet foreign debt.
"It has had no impact on Russian debt, save some marginal profit-taking," a trader at Moscow Narodny in London said.
"Generally, the market feels assured that the London Club deal is well-advanced and will reach reconciliation soon," the trader said.
Other dealers said the issue was a sidebar.
"This becomes an issue between Russia and the Ukraine," one London trader said.

Ukrainian deputies voted 233 to 70 to present Russia with a long list of conditions for ratification, including full information on money held by the Soviet central banking system when the Soviet Union broke up in 1991.
Later, Russia's deputy finance minister, Mikhail Kasyanov, told Reuters the issue would not affect Russia's debt agreements with the London and Paris Clubs.
"The Ukraine and Russia are going to have to sort out their relationship," a Deutsche Morgan Grenfell analyst in Frankfurt said. "They are forced to come up with a mutual solution."
A London-based analyst said the "more important story" was that the London Club deal was close to closing.
"It should get signed up by the end of April, with the deal out in May/June time," he said.
The Russian Vnesh U.S.$ RUVNUSLNS=RR was at around 84.375 at 1640 GMT versus a previous close of 84.500.
